added_lines: . offertory collection: thank you for your contribution to the offertory collection for sunday 11th october which amounted to €3,618.46. found: purse last weekend at cornamaddy. owner please contact st. mary’s parish office . this weekend’s anniversary masses saturday 17th october & sunday 18th october our lady, queen of peace sat 7:00 tom(big tom) o’donoghue - month’s memory sun 10:30 sinead cronin sun 12:00 shared mass: 1. bridie dunning 2. john & nuala o’meara 3. kieran & mary dolan st. mary’s sun 10:00 kathleen henson sun 12:00 doreen evans - month’s memory sun 6:00 mary kilmartin st. mary’s parish sund ay 18th october 2026 diocesan safeguarding: clergy, safeguarding representative, sacristans, volunteer leaders working with children – with altar servers, play & pray, john paul awards, etc who have not trained in the 5 training dates in july and september 2025 and july 2026 will need to complete this mandatory training. the next training session will take place on tuesday 20th october from 7-9 pm in the temperance hall longford. secular franciscan order: will be reciting the rosary at the franciscan graves this month. cornamagh cemetery on saturday 24th october and coosan cemetery on saturday 31st october. both at 11 am. all welcome. sfo meeting will take place in st. mary’s church after the 9:30am mass on tuesday 20th october. athlone

baptisms: we welcome into the christian community olivia brady, claudia o’reilly and lottie lynch, who were baptised last weekend. deaths: we pray for the happy repose of the soul of tom doherty, (cara court, & formerly kilbride) and andrew kelly (annaghearly), whose funerals took place during the week. may they rest in the peace of christ. community notices kiltoghert women’s group: join us for a presentation by dillon keane . who will speak about; how to start your own local walking group and how to plan fun social activities with other groups in the community, on wednesday 21st october at 8.30pm. all welcome the carrick historical society is pleased to announce an upcoming talk by carrick native dr heather laird (senior lecturer, ucc). dr laird will discuss the farming aspects of john mcgahern's writings, exploring themes from the post-revolution and post-civil war eras to current attitudes and practices. wednesday, october 21st, 8:00pm in st. george's/heritage centre (n41 kp62). contact/info:
